title: The Jacket Finally Fits: Williams Takes the Lot on the Lisbon Coast
title_candidates: Green at Last: Williams Completes the Set
An Eight at the First, Everything by the End
theme: Gregg Williams, three Trophies and never once a Green Jacket, spends four days on the Lisbon Coast winning both from the front — and takes the Jacket off the man who owns nine of them, David Mullin, with a course-record 82 in the Sintra hills as the exclamation mark.
tone: house — faithful, tongue-in-cheek, Ronay/Peck: dry, affectionate, anchored in the numbers, gentle ribbing of insiders
opening_hook: Open on Estoril's 1st, where Williams begins TEG 15 with a quadruple-bogey 8 (b25) — the least promising start imaginable to the most complete win of his TEG career — then set up the three-act climb: Act I the two new courses (R1–R2), Act II the course record at Penha Longa (R3), Act III the coronation at Oitavos (R4).
foreshadow: Williams starts with an 8 at Estoril's 1st and finishes the round with another at the 18th — the worst golf of his tournament happens on day one and costs him nothing
Mullin arrives as defending Trophy champion with nine Green Jackets and the standing 86 at Penha Longa from TEG 8 — the Jacket has essentially been his personal property
Mullin's eagle at West Cliffs' 15th is the only eagle anybody makes all tournament — remember which hole that is
Jon Baker arrives as the reigning Wooden Spoon holder, and there are two Bakers in the field

competitions.name: Trophy (Stableford)
competitions.winner_or_loser: Gregg Williams — 157 pts, by 21 from Stuart Neumann
competitions.how: Williams took the outright lead at R1 H4 and was never headed: 39, 40, then a 44-point round at Penha Longa that doubled the lead from 9 to 18 and ended the argument, before a comfortable 34 at Oitavos. Jon Baker (R1 H10) and John Patterson (R2 H3) briefly shared the top, but no lead change after R2 H3 and none at all in the final round.

competitions.name: Green Jacket (Gross)
competitions.winner_or_loser: Gregg Williams — +63, by 29 from Jon Baker
competitions.how: Williams went outright top on gross at R1 H11 and led by 8, 14, 17 and finally 29 — a margin that grew every single round. The 86 at Estoril came despite two quadruple bogeys; the 82 at Penha Longa was a new course record and a 14-shot improvement on his own last visit; the 91 at Oitavos was another personal best there. His first Green Jacket at the fifteenth attempt, taken from a nine-time holder.

competitions.name: Wooden Spoon
competitions.how: Baker was bottom of the field after both R1 and R2 but only fell to outright last at R3 H1 (b38), a double bogey at Penha Longa that flipped him from 5th to 6th and settled the matter — he stayed there for the remaining 53 holes. The damage was serial rather than singular: 13 shots gone in three holes at West Cliffs (b62), sextuple bogeys at West Cliffs' 6th and 17th (b09, b10), and Penha Longa's 14th (b11). The Spoon passes from Jon Baker to his brother.

headline_candidates: An Eight at the First, a Lead by the Last
Portugal's Oldest Club Meets TEG's Newest Ideas
Williams Bookends an 86 With Two Quadruple Bogeys
rounds.chosen_headline: An Eight at the First, a Lead by the Last
rounds.angle: Estoril, a new course for TEG: Williams opens with a quad at the 1st and closes with another at the 18th, and still leads both competitions by nightfall — the first hint that everyone else was going to have a harder day than he was.

headline_candidates: The Fifteenth Giveth and Taketh Away
Cynthia Dye's Dunes Take Thirteen Shots Off Alex Baker in Three Holes
rounds.chosen_headline: The Fifteenth Giveth and Taketh Away
rounds.angle: West Cliffs, also new, hands out the tournament's only eagle (Mullin, the par-5 15th) and a 10 to Williams on the very same hole — and still Williams stretches the Jacket lead from 8 to 14 while the rest of the field posts elevens.

headline_candidates: Williams Rewrites Penha Longa; Alex Baker Rewrites Himself
Fourteen Shots Better Than Last Time, and a Record Gone
rounds.angle: The decisive round: on TEG's second visit to Penha Longa, Williams's 82 breaks the course record of 86 that had survived six visits, is a personal-best gross round (+10) and 14 shots better than his own last trip — 44 points, the lead out to 18, tournament over. On the same hills Alex Baker slides to outright last at the 1st.

headline_candidates: Coronation on the Atlantic, Carnage at the First
Patterson's Ten, Mullin's Worst Day, Williams's Full Set
Oitavos Hands Out Personal Bests and One Very Bad Morning
rounds.chosen_headline: Coronation on the Atlantic, Carnage at the First
rounds.angle: Oitavos Dunes wrecks the first hole for Patterson (a 10) and Alex Baker (an 8) while Williams calmly posts 91 — another personal best there — to finish +63 and 157 points; Mullin, meanwhile, records the worst round of his TEG life, 16 shots worse than his last visit to the same links.

players.arc: Perennially thereabouts — 3rd, 2nd, 2nd, 3rd in the last four TEGs and never a Green Jacket in his life — Williams leads both competitions from R1 and turns a good week into a historic one with a course-record 82 at Penha Longa, finishing with the Trophy by 21 and his first Jacket by 29.

Defending Trophy champion and owner of nine Green Jackets arrives as the man to beat and leaves 29 shots adrift, his only eagle of the tournament at West Cliffs rendered a footnote by the worst round and worst gross round of his TEG career at Oitavos — though he did quietly set a personal best at Penha Longa, on the day someone else broke the record.

Reigning Wooden Spoon holder who escapes the family shame by handing it sideways to his brother, surviving an 11 at West Cliffs' 17th to take second in the Jacket on the back of personal bests at Penha Longa (85, six better) and Oitavos (94).

One prior Trophy and two runner-up finishes in the last four TEGs count for nothing as he assembles a catalogue of ruin — 13 shots in three holes at West Cliffs, sextuples at three separate courses — falls to outright last at R3's opening hole and stays there, taking the Spoon on 114 points with a one-shot personal best at Oitavos as his sole consolation.

Never a TEG winner and holder of two Wooden Spoons, Neumann finishes runner-up in the Trophy while simultaneously running up a 10 at Estoril's 15th, an 11 at West Cliffs' 13th and a 10 at its 6th — proof that Stableford forgives what gross never will, plus a seven-shot personal best at Penha Longa.
Briefly shares the Trophy lead at R2 H3 and produces the field's hottest run — 19 points in six holes at Penha Longa — before Oitavos opens with a 10 at the 1st and 10 shots lost in three holes.

venue_notes: TEG's 4th visit to the Lisbon Coast, October 2022, and a deliberately lopsided itinerary: two brand-new courses first (Estoril, Portugal's oldest club, a short tree-lined Mackenzie Ross parkland that punishes wandering; then Cynthia Dye's West Cliffs links at Obidos, 'World's Best New Course' 2017 and the week's demolition site), then two returns to TEG 8 territory — Penha Longa's Robert Trent Jones Jr mountain course in the Sintra hills for R3 and Arthur Hills's Oitavos Dunes on the Cascais coast for R4. Use the new/old split structurally: nobody had history to defend at Estoril or West Cliffs, and everybody had history to answer for at Penha Longa and Oitavos. Weekday references, if used at all, must be Saturday (R1), Sunday (R2), Monday (R3), Tuesday (R4).
course_history_notes: Penha Longa in R3 was a mass improvement on TEG 8: Williams 82 (14 better, new course record), Jon Baker 85 (6 better), Neumann 92 (7 better), Mullin 85 (a personal best by one).
Williams's 82 broke a Penha Longa record of 86 that had stood across six prior visits.
Mullin went the other way at Oitavos Dunes: 104 in R4 against his 88 there in TEG 8 — 16 shots worse.
Alex Baker's 103 at Oitavos was a personal best there by a single shot, and the only course PB he managed all tournament.
decisive_moments: Trophy: R3 at Penha Longa — Williams's 44-point round turns a 9-point lead into 18 with a round to play, and the Trophy stops being a contest.
Green Jacket: R1 H11 at Estoril — Williams goes outright top on gross and is never headed again, the lead growing 8 → 14 → 17 → 29.
Wooden Spoon: R3 H1 at Penha Longa — Alex Baker's double bogey drops him to outright last (b38), where he remains for the final 53 holes.

payoffs.seed: Williams's 8 at Estoril's 1st (and another at the 18th)
payoffs.resolves_in: Round 1 close and the Green Jacket section
payoffs.payoff: He still shoots 86, still leads gross by 8 by close of play, and never trails again — his worst golf of the tournament happens on day one and costs him precisely nothing.

payoffs.seed: Mullin's nine Jackets and the standing 86 at Penha Longa
payoffs.payoff: Williams's 82 takes the Penha Longa record off him in R3 (cr01), and Mullin closes with the worst round and worst gross round of his TEG career at Oitavos (b28, b29) — 29 shots behind on the Jacket he has won nine times.

payoffs.seed: Mullin's eagle at West Cliffs' 15th, the only eagle of TEG 15
payoffs.payoff: The tournament's rarest shot is neutralised the same afternoon — Williams takes a 10 at that exact hole (b13) and still leaves West Cliffs 9 points and 14 shots clear.

payoffs.seed: Jon Baker arrives as reigning Wooden Spoon holder, with his brother in the field
payoffs.resolves_in: How the three were decided / Wooden Spoon section
payoffs.payoff: Jon escapes to Jacket runner-up; Alex drops to outright last at R3 H1 (b38) and keeps the Spoon in the family on 114 points (b21).

vehicle_fit_response.note: Taken as a supporting frame — Alex Baker's seven blow-ups genuinely are an inventory rather than a collapse — but the report is framed on Williams's first Green Jacket in fifteen TEGs (origin) and the dethroning of Mullin, holder of nine (inversion); close_finish is false, so the 21/29-shot procession is texture, not frame.
